## Critique
- claim-1: Supported. Since \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the integral span of Schur functions outside \((n-r)^r\), the surviving \(\bar s_\lambda\) form an integral basis. Truncated Littlewood–Richardson multiplication is stated at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269].
- claim-2: Supported at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]. Writing \(G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}\), generation gives a surjection
  \[
  F:=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Ze_\rho\twoheadrightarrow Q,
  \qquad e_\rho\mapsto[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}].
  \]
  Indeed, modulo \(A_+J_v\), only the integral constant terms of coefficients in an \(A\)-linear expression survive.
- claim-3: The accepted task 292 supplies this internal proof dependency. Its maps audit correctly: on the full original variable lattice,
  \[
  T(A_{\lambda,\theta})=\bar s_\lambda\otimes\bar s_\theta
  \]
  is injective by claim-1, while [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 428-493] identifies row vectors with \(\mathrm{CP}\)-tensors. For a nonempty tall bottom partition \(\beta\),
  \[
  \mathrm{CP}(\bar s_\beta\otimes1)
  =\sum_{\mu\ne\varnothing}(-1)^{|\mu|+1}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}
    \mathrm{CP}(\bar s_\lambda\otimes\bar s_{\mu'})
  \]
  follows integrally from the antipode identity. Every nonzero summand yields an original wide partition
  \[
  (i+\mu'_1,\ldots,i+\mu'_j,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_a).
  \]
  The inequalities \(\mu'\subseteq a^b\), \(a+i\le n-r\), \(b\le j\), \(\lambda_1\le b\le i\), and \(a+j\le r\) verify every map and containment. Injectivity of \(T\) then gives equality of full-coordinate integral rows. No variable projection is used.
- claim-4: Established from claims 1–3. If \(0\ne x\in\ker(F\to Q)\), take a nonzero homogeneous component of degree \(ij+N\):
  \[
  \sum_{|\rho|=N}c_\rho\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}\in A_+J_v.
  \]
  Since \(J_v=AG_L\),
  \[
  A_+J_v=\sum_{\lambda\subseteq b^a}A_+\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)}.
  \]
  Homogeneity therefore expresses the right side using coefficients of degree \(N-|\lambda|>0\), hence only \(|\lambda|<N\). The left side is nonzero because its Schur classes are distinct basis elements. The source reduction [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 326-344], followed by claim-3, makes the associated system simultaneously have zero wide right sides and a nonzero tall right side, which is impossible. For \(N=0\), \((A_+J_v)_{ij}=0\); when \(a=0\), this also handles the sole generator. Thus \(F\to Q\) is injective.

## Required revisions
- No mathematical repair is required. The requested target is established:
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\cong
  \bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}].
  \]
  Claims 3–4 are internal proofs using accepted task 292, not independently source-backed claims. No \(G_L\)-to-\(G_R\) computation is used or scheduled.
